title: The affected selection as the task gate
desiredOutcome: A task's gate is the affected selection, after a re-measurement shows 0 misses over at least 20 commits; whole-tree scanners run once per phase and on push; CI stays inside its wall-time bound

findings.issue: contradicts task clause: "`time python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py` must finish in under 240 s wall on the owner's machine, twice, at least 20 minutes apart, on a quiet machine" (and the title, 'The sweep finishes under four minutes'). The diff does not meet it: the executor's own runs are 378.4 s and 492.3 s wall on a loaded machine (load 10-49), 519.5 s before, and its estimate for a quiet machine is 280-300 s. The task's own fallback clause ('If 240 s is still out of reach, say what the remaining critical path is ... and do not close the task as met') applies, and the executor does follow it: it does not claim the target and names the critical path (production git calls, measured as 10104 child processes in ar-block; other suites). So the report is honest, but the task as titled is NOT met and must not be closed as met.
findings.resolution: Close this task as partial (the in-process conversion and the split of ar-block), not as meeting 240 s. File a follow-up task that (a) memoises or batches the production git calls the profile named (_config.checkout_top / rev-parse per call, integrate-task refresh_records, drive-phase carry_git/tree_undescribed, _worktrees.admin_dir, _locks.lock_dir) and/or cuts the next-heaviest suites (test_audit_task, test_commit_task_work, test_stamp_verification, test__deps, test_close_phase), and (b) owns the two timed quiet-machine runs 20 minutes apart, since none of the five timed runs here was quiet.

findings.issue: The new runner is shared by almost every case in the suite, yet the five-row probe mutates the verbs and the sitecustomize fallback, never the runner itself. Nothing shown goes red if _restore_environ stops removing a verb's added variables (the lock token it hands children), if cwd or sys.argv are not restored, or if _exit_status maps a non-int exit code to 0. Process-global state leaking from one verb into the next is the one defect class in-process execution adds, and tests.add is none. Related fidelity gap: in-process the lock holder pid recorded by _locks._holder_pid is the live test process (and _locks.py:577 treats pid == getpid() as ours), so a case that depends on a lock left by a verb that died being read as holder-gone cannot be shown through an in-process verb. No row shows such a case still spawns a process.
findings.resolution: Add a small case in the suite (and a probe row each) that runs a stub script through _run_in_process which sets an environment variable, changes cwd, calls sys.exit('x') and sys.exit(3), and assert the environment, cwd, argv and exit codes after; and add a probe row that makes the runner leak the environment. For the pid point, either grep the converted cases for ones that rely on a verb's own pid being dead and route them through _needs_process, or state in the runner comment that holder-liveness is not exercised in-process.

findings.issue: The task said to re-record the figures the executor measured. The 120 block figures were not recorded by --record-costs; they were derived by scaling the darwin block seconds of one loaded run (run2, load 10-24) by 4913.6/2080.0, the old windows-latest suite figure over the darwin seconds of the baseline run (load 20-26). The three new blocks (ar5/ar9/ar18) and the suite figure 2665.5 therefore rest on two runs taken under different machine loads. These figures set per-block hang-detector timeouts and shard balance in CI, so an under-estimate on windows shows up as a spurious timeout and an over-estimate only as a slack deadline. It is disclosed in the platform note, and swd7 and bk5/tt5 are green.
findings.resolution: Re-record from a quiet darwin run (and a windows CI log via --costs-from-log) when the follow-up task takes its quiet-machine timings; until then leave the note as written.

findings.issue: The task asked for the mutations3 probe to be delivered as scratchpad/probe/mutations.py; it exists only at <scratchpad>/p1435/probe/mutations.py (6411 bytes) because the plan gate refused the path in the task tree. The red evidence (5 rows, ALL ROWS RED 04:39:16Z) therefore cannot be re-run from the commit.
findings.resolution: Have the orchestrator carry the file with the phase record, or record its path and digest in the task's notes; no code change.

findings.issue: The new test-support widening ignores a declared entry that is the unscoped sweep. select() returns `widen` for any changed file under a test directory that no arm picked, whatever the task's gate holds, so affected_steps never reaches left_to_run and instead adds every phase-gate entry the task did not declare as `affected/phase-gate:` steps. With a gate of [selftests] (or [selftests, lint]) in the dogfood plan, a change to tests/_harness.py now pulls validate, plugin-validate, gate, report, shots, interactive and vitest into the task run, browser gates included. But the reason for this widening is that every suite may depend on the support file, and `selftests` (python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py, the spelling with {paths} removed) already runs every suite. This works against the description's 'counts as already wide for the Python arm' and the phase outcome that whole-tree scanners run once per phase. It costs time but is not a correctness gap: the widened run is a superset.
findings.resolution: Treat the test-support widen as satisfied when a declared entry is the derived spelling with `{paths}` removed. That is the same word comparison left_to_run makes. Either have select() report support as its own reason (e.g. `widenSuites`) that affected_steps checks against the declared entries before adding the phase gate, or make the check in affected_steps. Add a case: gate [selftests] with only tests/_harness.py changed adds no phase-gate step and says which key covers it. Keep the case where a narrow path-scoped gate with the same change still widens.

findings.file: .github/sweep-costs.json:540-541 (and every figure above it); readers tools/sweep-selftests.py:196-208, :1567-1572 and .github/workflows/ci.yml:60-75
findings.issue: The cost table now says platform 'darwin' with 8 workers, where it used to hold windows-latest figures for 4 workers. Two things read it: CI's windows shard split and each job's hang-detector timeout. tools/sweep-selftests.py:206-208 and :1567-1572 still say the table 'is recorded from windows because that platform binds ... a darwin figure under-states a windows one'. The windows-to-darwin ratio is not even, and the split assumes it is. test__manifest_io went from 129.8 to 4.4 (about 30x), test__machine_paths from 32.2 to 0.2, test_integrate_task from 123.4 to 6.4, while most suites moved by about 3x. So the windows shards are now balanced on proportions that do not hold on windows. The ci.yml selftests bound estimate is also derived from this table. The phase outcome 'CI stays inside its wall-time bound' was never measured after the change. The executor did disclose this under CONSEQUENCE TO PUBLISH, and the task told it to re-record from the quiet runs.
findings.resolution: Before this lands, push the tree to a ci/ branch, dispatch CI, and read each windows selftests cell's longest line and wall time. Then re-record the table from those windows logs with `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py --costs-from-log <logs> --platform win32 --record-costs .github/sweep-costs.json`. These are still measured figures, not scaled ones, and they keep the windows-binding design the runner documents. If the darwin table is to stay, rewrite the two comments in tools/sweep-selftests.py and the ci.yml estimate so they say what the table now is.

findings.file: tests/test__config.py:3070-3216 (st1-st7, outside the declared files); task tests.gate
findings.issue: The memo's correctness cases (st1-st7) are in tests/test__config.py. That file is not among the task's declared files, and no tests.gate command selects it. The only gate is `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tests/test_drive_phase.py`, so the recorded gate run (2026-10-30T13:55:12Z.969e51, passed) shows nothing about the memo, test__locks, test__worktrees or test_integrate_task. The executor's 'full sweep green three times' and 'test__config 370/370' claims carry a stamp that `stamp-verification.py compare` grades stale (exit 1): head moved from c57e3f3c to abeac86b. The scopeDigest still agrees, but that digest does not cover tests/test__config.py. I ran `python3 tests/test__config.py --selftest` once in the task tree: exit 0, 370/370, st1-st7 PASS.
findings.resolution: Add tests/test__config.py to the task's files and list st1-st7 in tests.add. Add a gate command that selects the suites guarding the changed modules: `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tests/test__config.py tests/test__locks.py tests/test__worktrees.py tests/test_integrate_task.py tests/test_drive_phase.py`. Re-run the gate on the current tree so the claim carries a current stamp.

findings.issue: Suppose the combined `--show-toplevel` + fields question is refused and a repository stands above. git_place then asks a second time for the fields alone, whatever the refusal was, including a TimeoutExpired or a failure to start git. That doubles the worst-case wait. A hook path that asks a field list without --show-toplevel (`_shares_repository` and `path_tree` ask `--git-common-dir` alone) can now spend 5 s + 5 s, which equals the 10 s timeout hooks.json gives every hook. A killed guard lets the call through. In _worktrees the wait goes from 60 s to 120 s.
findings.resolution: Retry the fields-alone question only when the first refusal is git's bare/no-work-tree refusal: the reason line names a work tree, or a separate rev-parse --is-bare-repository says so. Do not retry on a timeout or an exception. Or hand the second ask whatever is left of the first one's timeout. Add a case with a stub `_ask_rev_parse` that times out and assert that it was called once.

findings.issue: The two witnesses check different things. A kept refusal is dropped when a bare-repository shape (HEAD + objects + refs) appears on the way up. A kept answer only checks for `.git` entries between the directory and its top (_inside_known_tree) and the identity of top/.git. So a kept answer survives two kinds of change. (a) A bare repository initialised in a directory between the asked directory and its top: git would then refuse or answer the bare repo, but the memo still hands back the old top. (b) A config-only change under an unchanged `.git` directory, such as `core.worktree` or `core.bare` set after the answer was kept. A directory's inode does not move when .git/config is edited. Both are rare, and a hook is one process per call. The drive process is long-lived, though, and the block comment says the witness covers 'a repository initialised between the directory and the top it had' without that limit.
findings.resolution: Have the answer witness walk with the same predicate as _no_repository_above, so the bare shape counts too. When top/.git is a directory, add .git/config's (st_ino, st_size, st_mtime_ns) to its identity. Otherwise state both limits in the block comment above _STANDING_FIELDS. Do not add GIT_CONFIG_COUNT to _DISCOVERY_ENV: the sweep runner sets it for every child, which would turn the memo off under test.

tasks.title: A task's gate is the affected selection, and no derived step re-runs what a declared key already runs in full
tasks.description: run-test-gate.py measures a task's declared non-suite entries plus the suites the selection names for its changed paths; an unrecognised path class widens to the phase gate and says so. A declared key whose command is the unscoped sweep (the dogfood plan's selftests) counts as already wide for the Python arm, so no affected/python or affected/related step is added beside it: today such steps re-run suites the key already ran. The recorded row commits with no override. Acceptance: (1) a task gate holding the full-sweep key adds no affected/python or affected/related step; (2) a narrow declared gate gets the affected suites for its changed paths and none for an unchanged tree; (3) an unrecognised path widens to the phase gate, saying so; (4) the green row commits without override; (5) the selection is used only after the miss-rate task's result is recorded with zero misses, or with each miss's path class widened to the full set.

tasks.title: Whole-tree scanners run once per phase and on push, never in a task's gate
tasks.description: The suites that lint the whole tree (TREE_SCANNERS in tools/affected.py) leave the per-task selection: a .py change no longer pulls them into a task's gate. The phase gate and verify.sh's per-run tier keep every one of them, so CI and sign-off still run them. Acceptance: (1) a task changing one .py selects no tree scanner; (2) the phase gate and verify.sh's per-run tier include every tree scanner; (3) tools/gate-parity.py is green; (4) CONTRIBUTING.md says where the scanners run.

Every row RED and restored: listing keeps blanket scanners -> a16, a16b, af27; scanners dropped everywhere (over-fire) -> a16b (also a15, a18b); listing drops edge-reached scanners (over-narrow) -> a16; --list-scanners one short -> a16c; parse reads no commands -> a16c, svr2b; sweep stops walking tools/ -> a16c, af28. The cost table belongs to P143.7 and was not re-recorded. test__gate_derive, test__refs, test_derive_phase_gate, bench-hooks, lints/_refs.py (via test__refs), prove-gates and measure-affected-miss are all green. The last still reads the default --json selection, so its misses still count the scanners. verify.sh: --affected reads the default output, unchanged; gate-parity's affected_dispatch is green. gate-parity.py: parse_verify_list only gains a key; ci.yml, _areas.py, test_audit_task, bench-hooks, _output_lints and measure-affected-miss read no changed key, and affected.py is now a new reader of 'commands'. For the plan: (a) test__affected_tests.py now calls _output.py_files, so it is itself a derived tree scanner (it appears in --list-scanners). (b) derive-phase-gate.py runs the same listing.related for a phase's importer arm. This plan sets no meta.phaseGate.mode, so the phase gate is testGate (selftests). If a derived phase gate is ever enforced, it will not carry the blanket scanners unless meta.phaseGate.always or the wide gate does. (c) The miss measurement measures the narrowed run with scanners, not the task listing; a scanner red that a task listing leaves out is deferred to sign-off by design, not counted as a miss. TDD note: I read affected.py's select()/reach_graph() and _affected_tests.select() before writing the cases, because I needed the API the cases call.
outcome.descriptive: A task's gate no longer pulls in every whole-tree scanner for any .py change. Those suites and tools run in the phase gate's unscoped sweep and verify.sh's per-run tier, and cases keep that true.

tasks.title: The affected selector reaches a hook or suite through an assembled path, and the measurement measures a commit that touches its own runner
tasks.description:
The affected selector pinned at d36d84e8 was re-measured over 20 commits with `tools/measure-affected-miss.py --rev d36d84e8 --commits 26 --selector <tools/affected.py at d36d84e8> --ci-since 2026-10-20`. It missed suites, so the affected selection cannot yet be a task's gate. Fix what it missed, and make the measurement able to measure every commit:

1. An import-time raise in plugins/audit/scripts/governance/drive-phase.py and plugins/audit/scripts/manifest/_manifest_*.py (commits d36d84e8, 0b856d0c, 862b4941) turned `.claude/hooks/guard-release.py` and `.claude/hooks/arm-release-bypass.py` red. The selection named neither. Those hooks reach plugin scripts through a path assembled from string pieces (`os.path.join("plugins", "audit", "scripts", ...)` held in a module constant) and a subprocess. The reach graph reads a literal path only. Make it read a path assembled from literal pieces, directly or through a module-level constant, the same way it reads a literal. Do this in `.claude/hooks/` exactly as in `tests/` and `tools/`. Add a case per shape that is red on today's selector.
2. An import-time raise at a1891691 (which changed tools/affected.py and tools/measure-affected-miss.py) turned `tests/test_derive_phase_gate.py` red, unselected. Find the edge the graph does not read and fix it by the same rule as in 1, not by a hand-listed suite. Add a case.
3. Five commits read could-not-measure (089036e0, 9eeea6d5, 0544c08c, d4a26f13, 46a6e095). In each, the mutation lands in `tools/sweep-selftests.py` or `tools/lints/_output_lints.py`, so the runner doing the measuring dies at import before any suite runs. Run the mutated tree's suites under an unmutated copy of the runner and of the lints it imports, so those commits are measured. The runner's own suite still sees the mutation. A case: a commit touching the runner is measured, not skipped.
4. Say in your outcome whether CI's Windows miss on 94a097d7 (tests/_harness.py, CRLF; fixed since) is a selection miss or a platform-only red that a posix selection cannot see. If it is the latter, the measurement reports it apart from selection misses.

Who depends on these files: tools/affected.py is called by tools/verify.sh --affected and by plugins/audit/scripts/governance/_affected_tests.py (P143.1 makes it the task gate). tools/measure-affected-miss.py is read by tools/lints/_output_lints.py (a row near the prose-number exemptions). Run both tools' --selftest and tests/test__affected_tests.py, tests/test__output_lints.py and tests/test_derive_phase_gate.py.

Deliver scratchpad/probe/mutations.py (mutations3 engine): one row per fix that removes it, each expected red.
No F/P/BUG ids in comments.

tasks.title: The sweep finishes under four minutes: the drive's suite calls its verbs in-process where no case asserts the process boundary
tasks.description:
`time python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py` must finish in under 240 s wall on the owner's machine, twice, at least 20 minutes apart, on a quiet machine. P142 measured 385.3 s and 385.4 s. The lower bound under perfect packing was about 339 s: summed slot-seconds over the sweep's slots. tests/test_drive_phase.py alone is the largest share, because it starts one process per verb call. Re-derive both figures with the sweep's loud output before you start; do not trust these.

Cut test_drive_phase.py's cost by its structure. Call the drive's verbs in-process, through the module the suite already loads, wherever a case does not assert on process behaviour (exit codes, stdio encoding, signal handling, the subprocess boundary itself). Keep a subprocess case for each of those that does. Each converted case must still fail on the bug it guards. Pick a sample of converted cases, mutate the guarded code, show them red, and deliver scratchpad/probe/mutations.py (mutations3 engine).

Then re-record the darwin figures you measured. Report the two timed runs with their start times. If 240 s is still out of reach, say what the remaining critical path is, with the numbers the sweep prints, and do not close the task as met.

Who depends on this: tools/sweep-selftests.py reads the suite's STAGES table for its blocks and .github/sweep-costs.json for its timeouts. tests/_harness.py's staged_main runs the blocks. No F/P/BUG ids in comments.

outcome.technical:
WHAT CHANGED. tests/test_drive_phase.py: (1) `_load` now replaces every loaded driver's `run_verb` with `_in_process_verbs(module)`, which runs each verb's script as `__main__` in the block's interpreter via `_run_in_process` (own argv, cwd, environment, byte-backed stdin/stdout/stderr whose codec and error handler mirror what a child interpreter picks; SystemExit mapped to the exit status; an escaping exception becomes a traceback on stderr and exit 1; sys.stdin/out/err, argv, path, cwd and os.environ restored afterwards) and decodes the bytes with the module's own `_verb_text`/`_record_text`, logging the same `ctx['log']` entry. (2) The suite's own `_verb` (submit, audit-lock status, audit-task, run-test-gate ... called by cases) goes through the same runner. A script that defines `run_verb` (the driver's own `submit`) has it routed in-process too: `_script_parts` splits each script into body and trailing main guard (AST, memo keyed by path+mtime_ns+size) so the patch lands before the command line runs. (3) `_needs_process` keeps a verb a real process when a fixture planted a `sitecustomize` on PYTHONPATH (pinned clock `sc4/sc4b`, Windows stdout) or the case replaced the module's own `subprocess` (the stdin-bytes case). Process-boundary cases untouched and still spawned by hand: ds9/ds9w (command-line exit status), the CRLF brief case (stdout pipe bytes), al-block (children under the ASCII locale). (4) ar-block, the single heaviest block, was cut where no later group reads an earlier binding: new STAGES rows ar5-block, ar9-block, ar18-block placed right after ar-block (replay order unchanged), each loading a fresh driver; sb1 (stage_reach) green. (5) Module docstring and the pinned-clock comment rewritten to say what the suite now does. .github/sweep-costs.json: test_drive_phase.py's 120 block figures and its suite figure re-recorded from the darwin run2 block seconds scaled by 4913.6/2080.0 (the old windows-latest suite figure over the darwin seconds the baseline run measured) -> suite figure 4913.6 -> 2665.5, heaviest block ar-block 596.3 -> ar18-block 196.8; platform note extended to say so. Written in the recorder's own format (json indent 1, sorted, figure = round(sum of blocks,1)); swd7 (byte-for-byte rewrite) green. Edit tool accepted on this path by the plan gate; the block lines were then copied in from the generated file.

MEASUREMENTS (darwin, 10 cores, 8 sweep slots, machine shared with another project's Playwright run; `uptime` load averages at start->end of each run; logs base1.log, run1.log, run2.log, run3.log under <scratchpad>/p1435/). `time python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py` (sum = summed slot-seconds the sweep printed; /8 = the perfect-packing bound):
- base1 BEFORE, started 2026-10-30T03:11:32Z, load 19.67->26.44: real 519.48 s, user 1923.6 + sys 1154.3 s; sum 4116.5 (/8 = 514.6); drive suite 2080.9, ar-block 303.7 (longest job); others 2035.6. exit 0, 193/193 files, 17607 cases.
- run1 in-process verbs, before the ar split, started 03:47:51Z, load 14.18->34.94 (peak ~49): real 502.57 s, user 1328.8 + sys 1077.9; sum 3974.5 (/8 = 496.8); drive 1505.9, ar-block 246.6; others 2468.6. exit 0, 17607 cases.
- run2 with the split, started 04:08:34Z (20m43s after run1), load 10.62->24.34: real 378.39 s, user 1295.7 + sys 1056.1; sum 2979.5 (/8 = 372.4); drive 1129.7, longest job tests/test__output_lints.py 92.4 s, drive's heaviest block ar18-block 83.3; others 1849.8. exit 0, 17607 cases.
- run3 final tree, started 04:28:41Z (20m07s after run2), load 11.71->24.59 (~44 mid-run): real 492.27 s, user 1348.7 + sys 1113.2; sum 3899.7 (/8 = 487.5); drive 1544.4, longest job tests/test__output_lints.py 94.2; others 2355.3. exit 0, 17607 cases.
The load-robust figure is child CPU (user+sys): 3078.0 s before vs 2406.7 / 2351.8 / 2461.9 s after (about 22-24 percent less). The drive suite's share of the summed slot-seconds went from 50.5 percent to 37.9 / 37.9 / 39.6 percent.

240 s NOT MET, AND NOT CLAIMABLE FROM THIS MACHINE: every run was loaded (1-minute load 10-49 on 10 cores). Every run's wall sits at its own perfect-packing bound (sum/8 within 2 percent of real), so the remaining critical path is the summed slot-seconds, not any single job: after the change no job is longer than about 95 s. Even run2's lightest-load figures leave the other suites alone at 1849.8 slot-s, which is 231 s over 8 slots before the drive suite's 1129.7 is added. What remains in the drive suite is git, not Python: a profile of ar-block after the change (scratchpad prof.py / who.py) counted 10104 child processes, 101.7 s of its 109.9 s wall in children, almost all git from PRODUCTION code (git rev-parse 3713 calls 32.5 s, ls-files 1648 15.1 s, diff 1068 10.4 s, status 722 7.8 s; top callers integrate-task.py refresh_records, drive-phase.py carry_git/carry_commit/tree_undescribed, _worktrees.admin_dir/tree_root, _locks.lock_dir, _config.checkout_top re-running rev-parse per call). Those files are outside this task's scope. Next-heaviest suites in run2: test_audit_task.py 274.8, test_commit_task_work.py 171.3, test_stamp_verification.py 168.0, test__deps.py 130.6, test_close_phase.py 121.6. A quiet machine still has to: run `time python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py` twice, at least 20 minutes apart, and record wall, child CPU and the sum the sweep prints. From P142's quiet 385 s and the measured reduction, the estimate is roughly 280-300 s, which is above 240. Reaching 240 needs the production git calls memoised or batched (or other suites cut); that is a follow-up task, not this one.

tasks.title: The sweep finishes under four minutes on a quiet machine: production git calls are memoised or batched, and the timings are taken quiet
tasks.description:
The previous task moved the drive suite's verbs in-process (child CPU of a full sweep down about 22-24 percent, longest job from about 304 s to about 94 s), but a full `time python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py` still took 378-502 s on a loaded machine, against the target of under 240 s. Its profile of the heaviest drive block (ar-block) counted 10104 child processes, 101.7 s of its 109.9 s wall in children, nearly all git from production code: `git rev-parse` 3713 calls (32.5 s), `ls-files` 1648 (15.1 s), `diff` 1068 (10.4 s), `status` 722 (7.8 s). Named callers: `_config.checkout_top` (rev-parse per call), integrate-task.py `refresh_records`, drive-phase.py `carry_git` / `carry_commit` / `tree_undescribed`, `_worktrees.admin_dir`, `_locks.lock_dir`.

Do:
1. Measure first (choosing-what-to-optimize): rank the callers by the git time they cause across a whole sweep, not one block, and say which ones pay.
2. Cut the calls that pay: one shared, explicitly invalidated memo for answers that cannot change within one process (a checkout's top level, its git dir, a worktree's admin dir), or a batched call where one git invocation can answer several questions. One mechanism shared by every caller, not a per-caller cache; a cached answer must never outlive a change that can alter it (a worktree added or removed, a checkout moved), and the case for that is red-first.
3. If the target still needs it, cut the next-heaviest suites' wall (test_audit_task, test_commit_task_work, test_stamp_verification, test__deps, test_close_phase) by the same rule, measured.
4. The in-process runner the previous task added to tests/test_drive_phase.py (`_run_in_process`) gets a case: a stub script that sets an environment variable, changes cwd, calls sys.exit('x') and sys.exit(3) - assert environment, cwd, argv and exit statuses after. State in the runner's comment that lock-holder liveness is not exercised in-process, or route cases relying on a dead verb's pid through `_needs_process`.
5. Timings: `time python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py` twice, at least 20 minutes apart, on a QUIET machine (no Playwright, sweep or browser gate anywhere; print `uptime` beside each). Under 240 s both times is the target; if the machine cannot be made quiet, say so and do not claim it. Re-record .github/sweep-costs.json from the quiet runs (`--record-costs`), not by scaling.

Who depends on these files: every hook and script that resolves the checkout through _config; integrate-task.py and drive-phase.py are the drive's write path (tests/test_drive_phase.py, tests/test_integrate_task.py, tests/test_commit_task_work.py); _locks is read by every guard. Answer each in the outcome. Deliver scratchpad/probe/mutations.py (mutations3 engine), one row per memo whose invalidation it removes, each expected red. No F/P/BUG ids in comments.
